Don Fandetti
Managing Director, Wells Fargo
Okay. Just more generally in multifamily, are you seeing borrower pressure with higher rates?
Priyanka Garg
EVP of Portfolio and Asset Management, Claros Mortgage Trust
Yeah. Yeah, absolutely, of course. That's exactly why we made that shift in credit ratings on those four properties, because we have a huge multifamily exposure. We are very focused on monitoring all of those and making sure that borrowers are being successful in an environment where they have negative leverage. They are all doing the right thing. They believe in their thesis. They're putting in additional capital. We have yet to see cracks in their business plans because we're a transitional lender. We're still seeing NOI increase generally across the board. We're optimistic that the borrowers will be able to refinance this out over time, but we are monitoring it very closely. Again, that was the reason for the migration on the handful of loans that we moved to a four.
Don Fandetti
Managing Director, Wells Fargo
Got it. Really quickly, we've seen some other companies selling office loans. Are you looking at that option as well?
Priyanka Garg
EVP of Portfolio and Asset Management, Claros Mortgage Trust
I'll start, and then Richard, you might wanna jump in here. We're gonna look at all options available to us. As Richard said in his remarks, there are gonna be moments where we're gonna say, "Okay, we wanna exit the loan." There are gonna be moments where we say, "We like our basis." That example being the REO asset in New York that we just took on 30 June 2023, and which has an office component, but we like our basis there, and we think we have a great business plan. There are going to be other loans where we're gonna say, "You know what? We don't think that it makes sense to try to take ownership of it. We don't think we can add value specifically. In which case, we might look to exit loans, but nothing on our radar as we sit here today. Richard?
Richard Mack
CEO and Chairman, Claros Mortgage Trust
Look, yeah, let me just add as a general statement that, you know, everything that we own is kind of for sale. We are constantly looking at what is the value going forward that we think we can create. If we think a sale is better, we're gonna sell, and if we think we can create value and really in this environment, equity-like returns, holding an asset, or taking it REO, then we will.
Don Fandetti
Managing Director, Wells Fargo
Thank you.

Our next question comes from Vilas Abraham from UBS. Vilas, your line is now open. Please go ahead.
Vilas Abraham
Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Hey, everybody. Thanks for taking the question. Can you talk a little bit more about the liquidity trends? Cash was down quarter-over-quarter, also quarter-to-date. Vilas Abraham
Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Okay.
Mike McGillis

You know, all I have to say on that, any liquidity we do have is really gonna be deployed to maximize long-term shareholder value. That's our critical focus in everything we do.
Vilas Abraham
Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
On that REO property, do you plan to keep that on an unlevered basis, or would you put any financing on that given the quality of the collateral there?
Priyanka Garg
EVP of Portfolio and Asset Management, Claros Mortgage Trust
Hi, it's Priyanka. I'll jump in there. We're definitely gonna look at potentially putting on financing. It's really gonna depend on leverage levels and pricing. Vilas Abraham
Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Okay. Priyanka, maybe you could answer this one. On maturity defaults, you know, around $400 million or so, and that's outside of the kind of official non-accrual bucket, and that's kind of unchanged, I think, quarter over quarter. But our goal is to allow borrowers to execute on their business plan and monetize when they can. Of the $400 million that you mentioned, half of those loans are actually under transaction of some sort under term sheet or LOI, and part of the number that Mike just referred to where we might see some repayments in the H2. Obviously, it's a very uncertain environment, and we don't know where that'll end up. We're, you know, we're gonna monitor those, and in the interim, we're coming up with Plans B, C, and D in terms of other various paths to resolution. We're highly focused on it. You know, at the end of the day, it's all about the basis and then are we comfortable stepping in or not, which the answer to all of those is yes.
Vilas Abraham
Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Okay. Richard, this may be last one from me for you. We touched on this a little bit in your opening comments in terms of transaction volumes. Mike McGillis
President and Director, Claros Mortgage Trust
Yeah. This is Mike. Richard unfortunately got dropped from the call, and he's trying to get back on. Yeah. The buyer pools are obviously a lot smaller, so in terms of the bid-ask, you're not seeing prices being pushed up as much 'cause of multiple parties bidding. We continue to see strong pricing in the multifamily, industrial, and even hospitality markets as well. The volumes are way down. Vilas Abraham

Jade Rahmani
Managing Director, KBW
Lastly, just the Virgin Islands hospitality asset. I think last quarter you said there were bids for the debt above

Those bids were out there. Obviously, that was a very different capital markets environment. While we think this is a very attractive development site, it's just not the right time to monetize the investment. That said, we think the basis makes sense, and that's why it continues to be rated a four. We're gonna, you know, we continue to evaluate the paths forward with or without the borrower. Our path is gonna really be driven by the goal of maximizing shareholder value in the long term there. This is not the right moment to monetize that opportunity.
Richard Mack
CEO and Chairman, Claros Mortgage Trust
Thank you.
Operator
Our next question comes from Sarah Barcomb from BTIG. Sarah, your line is open. Please go ahead.
Sarah Barcomb
Commercial Mortgage and Specialty Finance Analyst, BTIG
Hi, everyone. Jai Agarwal
CFO, Claros Mortgage Trust
Sorry, this is Jai. Yes, you know, you are right. With the rising interest rate environment, we are in active dialogue with our lenders, and we actively monitor our covenants. We are comfortable that we are going to meet our financing covenants. To the extent we need to be proactive about modifying some of those, we will go ahead and do that.
Sarah Barcomb
Commercial Mortgage and Specialty Finance Analyst, BTIG
Okay. I was also hoping you could speak, maybe more thematically on what you're seeing on the ground in your construction book. How's the labor market there? Are you seeing more projects get certificates of occupancy? Any color you can give on the ground up exposure?
Priyanka Garg
EVP of Portfolio and Asset Management, Claros Mortgage Trust
Yeah. Hi. Hi, Sarah, it's Priyanka. I'll take that one. We're really happy with our construction exposure. Of those assets that have recently become operating assets, two out of eight of them are working on sales and refinancings, and the others are really going through a lease-up process right now. We've been really happy with that performance and we've always liked our construction exposure, you know, really for two reasons. One, our sponsors are gonna have best-in-class real estate upon completion, which is gonna fare better in this uncertain environment. Certainly, we're seeing that with the two assets that are right now being sold and refinanced. Two, we have much better structure about. You know, we get to re-underwrite the asset monthly. Borrowers are rebalancing monthly. They're contributing equity as needed. Of course, we have completion guarantees from really creditworthy sponsors. We've been really happy with that exposure, and it's played out as we would've expected.
Sarah Barcomb
Commercial Mortgage and Specialty Finance Analyst, BTIG
Thank you.
Operator
We currently have no further questions, so I'd like to hand the call back to Richard Mack for closing remarks. Richard, please go ahead.
Richard Mack
CEO and Chairman, Claros Mortgage Trust
Thank you, and thank you all for joining us today. I would summarize kind of how we see managing our business as focusing every day on creating long-term shareholder value. To do that, we're going to be opportunistic when we can, and we're staffed to be. We are organized to take assets back, if necessary, sell them, refinance them, and just be opportunistic around creating shareholder value for the long term. You know, that is a dynamic process as we manage our liquidity versus opportunity, and something that, you know, we're working on every day. We think that the process that we're undergoing and the value we've created already in some of the REO and some of the other actions we've taken working with borrowers is gonna pay dividends, so to speak. We gonna continue to increase value over the long term. Thanks all for joining, and we will look forward to our next earnings call.
Operator
Ladies and gentlemen, this concludes today's call. Thank you for joining. You may now disconnect your lines. Thank you.
